metadata.source: Śabdālaṃkāradoṣavibhāga Die Unterscheidung der Lautfiguren und der Fehler. Kritische Ausgabe des dritten Kapitels von Daṇḍins Poetik Kāvyādarśa und der tibetischen Übertragung Sñan ṅag me loṅ samt dem Sanskrit-Kommentar des Ratnaśrījñāna, dem tibetischen Kommentar des Dpaṅ Blo gros brtan pa und einer deutschen Übersetzung des Sanskrit-Grundtextes. Von Dragomir Dimitrov. Wiesbaden 2011. (Veröffentlichungen der Helmuth von Glasenapp-Stiftung, Monographien 2).

children.text: avyapetavyapetātmā vyāvṛttir varṇasaṃhateḥ /
children.translated_text: The repetition of a group of syllables, whether with identical or different meaning,

children.text: yamakaṃ tac ca pādānām ādimadhyāntagocaram // KDd_3.1 //
children.translated_text: is <s>yamaka</s> (rhyming repetition); and it occurs at the beginning, middle, and end of verse-quarters. || KDd 3.1 ||

children.text: ekadvitricatuṣpādayamakānāṃ vikalpanāḥ /
children.translated_text: The varieties of <s>yamaka</s> occurring in one, two, three, and four verse-quarters

children.text: ādimadhyāntamadhyāntamadhyādyādyantasarvataḥ // KDd_3.2 //
children.translated_text: are: at the beginning, middle, end, middle-and-end, middle-and-beginning, beginning-and-end, and everywhere. || KDd 3.2 ||

children.text: atyantabahavas teṣāṃ bhedāḥ saṃbhedayonayaḥ /
children.translated_text: Their varieties, born of combinations, are exceedingly numerous;

children.text: sukarā duṣkarāś caiva darśyante tatra ke cana // KDd_3.3 //
children.translated_text: some that are easy and some that are difficult are shown here. || KDd 3.3 ||

children.text: mānena mānena sakhi praṇayo bhūt priye jane /
children.translated_text: O friend, through honor upon honor, love arose in the beloved;

children.text: khaṇḍitā kaṇṭham āśliṣya tam eva kuru satrapam // KDd_3.4 //
children.translated_text: the offended one—embracing his neck, make him ashamed. || KDd 3.4 ||

children.text: meghanādena haṃsānāṃ madano madanodinā /
children.translated_text: By the sound of clouds, <s>Madana</s> (the god of love), exalted by the maddening season,

children.text: nunnamānaṃ manaḥ strīṇāṃ saha ratyā vigāhate // KDd_3.5 //
children.translated_text: enters the bowed-down minds of women together with passion. || KDd 3.5 ||

children.text: rājanvatyaḥ prajā jātā bhavantaṃ prāpya sāṃpratam /
children.translated_text: The subjects have become possessed of a king, having attained you at this time,

children.text: caturaṃ caturambhodhiraśanorvīkaragrahe // KDd_3.6 //
children.translated_text: O clever one, who holds in hand the earth girdled by four oceans. || KDd 3.6 ||

children.text: araṇyaṃ kaiś cid ākrāntam anyaiḥ sadma divaukasām /
children.translated_text: The forest was overrun by some, and the abode of the gods by others—

children.text: padātirathanāgāśvarahitair ahitais tava // KDd_3.7 //
children.translated_text: by your enemies devoid of infantry, chariots, elephants, and horses. || KDd 3.7 ||

children.text: madhuraṃ madhur ambhojavadane vada netrayoḥ /
children.translated_text: O lotus-faced one, sweetly speak something sweet; upon the eyes

children.text: vibhramaṃ bhramarabhrāntyā viḍambayati kiṃ nv idam // KDd_3.8 //
children.translated_text: does this, through the delusion of resemblance to bees, mock their movement? || KDd 3.8 ||

children.text: vāraṇo vā raṇoddāmo hayo vā smara durdharaḥ /
children.translated_text: Whether the elephant mighty in battle, or the horse difficult to restrain—

children.text: na yato nayato 'ntaṃ nas tad aho vikramas tava // KDd_3.9 //
children.translated_text: that which brings us no end—ah, such is your valor! || KDd 3.9 ||

children.text: rājitair ājitaikṣṇyena jīyate tvādṛśair nṛpaiḥ /
children.translated_text: By kings like you who have conquered sharpness with their radiance,

children.text: nīyate ca punas tṛptiṃ vasudhā vasudhārayā // KDd_3.10 //
children.translated_text: the earth is conquered and again brought to satisfaction through a stream of wealth. || KDd 3.10 ||

children.text: karoti sahakārasya kalikotkalikottaram /
children.translated_text: The cry of the intoxicated cuckoo causes,

children.text: manmano manmano 'py eṣa mattakokilanisvanaḥ // KDd_3.11 //
children.translated_text: in the heart of my beloved, wave upon wave of budding desire even beyond the mind's desire. || KDd 3.11 ||

children.text: kathaṃ tvadupalambhāśāvihatāv iha tādṛśī /
children.translated_text: How could such a condition, struck by the hope of obtaining you—

children.text: avasthā nālam āroḍhum aṅganām aṅganāśinī // KDd_3.12 //
children.translated_text: a condition that destroys the limbs of women—fail to be reached? || KDd 3.12 ||

children.text: nigṛhya netre karṣanti bālapallavaśobhinā /
children.translated_text: Restraining their eyes, the young women adorned with tender shoots draw

children.text: taruṇā taruṇān kliṣṭān alino nalinonmukhāḥ // KDd_3.13 //
children.translated_text: the tormented young men; bee-free, lotus-faced. || KDd 3.13 ||

children.text: viśadā viśadāmattasārase sārase jale /
children.translated_text: In the clear water where <s>sārasa</s> (cranes) are intoxicated, in the fine pool,

children.text: kurute kuruteneyaṃ haṃsī mām antakāmiṣam // KDd_3.14 //
children.translated_text: this female swan makes me food for Death. || KDd 3.14 ||

children.text: viṣamaṃ viṣam anveti madanaṃ madanandanaḥ /
children.translated_text: Terrible poison follows love; the delight of <s>Madana</s>—

children.text: sahendukalayāpoḍhamalayā malayānilaḥ // KDd_3.15 //
children.translated_text: the <s>Malaya</s> breeze, bearing moonlight and mountain fragrance. || KDd 3.15 ||

children.text: māninī mā ninīṣus te niṣaṅgatvam anaṅga me /
children.translated_text: O proud one, do not, O <s>Anaṅga</s> (Cupid), seek to impose the quiver upon me;

children.text: hāriṇī hāriṇī śarma tanutāṃ tanutāṃ yataḥ // KDd_3.16 //
children.translated_text: let the doe-eyed enchantress spread happiness, for she is of slender form. || KDd 3.16 ||

children.text: jayatā tvanmukhenāsmān akathaṃ na kathaṃ jitam /
children.translated_text: By your victorious face, how have we not been thoroughly vanquished?

children.text: kamalaṃ kam alaṃkurvad alimad dali matpriye // KDd_3.17 //
children.translated_text: The lotus—adorning whom, with its bees—O my beloved! || KDd 3.17 ||

children.text: ramaṇī ramaṇīyā me pāṭalāpāṭalāṃśukā /
children.translated_text: My beloved is charming, wearing a rose-colored garment;

children.text: vāruṇīvāruṇībhūtasaurabhā saurabhāspadam // KDd_3.18 //
children.translated_text: her fragrance having become like wine, she is the very abode of sweet fragrance. || KDd 3.18 ||

children.text: iti pādādiyamakam avyapetaṃ vikalpitam /
children.translated_text: Thus the <s>yamaka</s> at the beginning of the verse-quarter, of the non-disjoint (<s>avyapeta</s>) type, has been illustrated;

children.text: vyapetasyāpi varṇyante vikalpās tasya ke cana // KDd_3.19 //
children.translated_text: some varieties of the disjoint (<s>vyapeta</s>) type are also described. || KDd 3.19 ||

children.text: madhur eṇadṛśāṃ mānaṃ madhureṇa sugandhinā /
children.translated_text: The pride of the doe-eyed women, by the sweet, fragrant

children.text: sahakārodgamenaiva śabdaśeṣaṃ kariṣyati // KDd_3.20 //
children.translated_text: emergence of the mango alone, will be reduced to a mere name. || KDd 3.20 ||

children.text: karo 'titāmro rāmāṇāṃ tantrītāḍanavibhramam /
children.translated_text: The very red hand of the women, the playful striking of the lute-string—

children.text: karoti serṣyaṃ kānte vā śravaṇotpalatāḍanam // KDd_3.21 //
children.translated_text: it jealously imitates; or it imitates the striking of the ear-lotus by the beloved. || KDd 3.21 ||

children.text: sakalāpollasanayā kalāpinyānu nṛtyate /
children.translated_text: With the dancing of the peahen whose full plumage shimmers,

children.text: meghālī nartitā vātaiḥ sakalāpo vimuñcati // KDd_3.22 //
children.translated_text: the line of clouds, made to dance by the winds, releases all its waters. || KDd 3.22 ||

children.text: svayam eva galanmānakali kāmini te manaḥ /
children.translated_text: O desirable woman, your heart, already melting with the passion of dissolving pride—

children.text: kalikām atha nīpasya dṛṣṭvā kāṃ nu spṛśed daśām // KDd_3.23 //
children.translated_text: upon seeing the bud of the <s>nīpa</s> (kadamba) tree, what state would it reach? || KDd 3.23 ||

children.text: āruhyākrīḍaśailasya candrakāntasthalīm imām /
children.translated_text: Having ascended this moonstone terrace of the pleasure-mountain,

children.text: nṛtyaty eṣa lasaccārucandrakāntaḥ śikhāvalaḥ // KDd_3.24 //
children.translated_text: this peacock, beautiful in the splendid moonlight, dances. || KDd 3.24 ||

children.text: uddhṛtā rājakād urvī dhriyate 'dya bhujena te /
children.translated_text: The earth, lifted from a wicked king, is now upheld by your arm;

children.text: varāheṇoddhṛtā yāsau varāher uparisthitā // KDd_3.25 //
children.translated_text: she who was lifted by <s>Varāha</s> (the Boar incarnation) rests above the Boar. || KDd 3.25 ||

children.text: kareṇa te raṇeṣv antakareṇa dviṣatāṃ hatāḥ /
children.translated_text: By your hand, which makes an end of enemies in battles,

children.text: kareṇavaḥ kṣaradraktā bhānti saṃdhyāghanā iva // KDd_3.26 //
children.translated_text: the elephants, streaming with blood, shine like twilight clouds. || KDd 3.26 ||

children.text: parāgatarurājīva vātair dhvastā bhaṭaiś camūḥ /
children.translated_text: Like a row of retreating trees, the army was scattered by soldiers and winds;

children.text: parāgatam iva kvāpi parāgatatam ambaram // KDd_3.27 //
children.translated_text: and the sky became as if retreating somewhere, thick with pollen. || KDd 3.27 ||

children.text: pātu vo bhagavān viṣṇuḥ sadā navaghanadyutiḥ /
children.translated_text: May Lord <s>Viṣṇu</s>, always having the splendor of a fresh cloud, protect you—

children.text: sa dānavakuladhvaṃsī sadānavaradantihā // KDd_3.28 //
children.translated_text: He, the destroyer of the <s>Dānava</s> (demon) clan, the ever-generous slayer of great elephants. || KDd 3.28 ||

children.text: kam aleḥ samakeśaṃ te kamalerṣyākaraṃ mukham /
children.translated_text: Your face, rivaling the lotus, unmatched—causes jealousy in lotuses;

children.text: kam alekhyaṃ karoṣi tvaṃ kamalevonmadiṣṇuṣu // KDd_3.29 //
children.translated_text: whom do you render a mere painting, among those intoxicated by the lotus? || KDd 3.29 ||

children.text: mudā ramaṇam anvītam udāramaṇibhūṣaṇāḥ /
children.translated_text: With joy following their beloved, adorned with generous jewels,

children.text: madabhramaddṛśaḥ kartum adabhrajaghanāḥ kṣamāḥ // KDd_3.30 //
children.translated_text: with eyes bewildered by passion, with ample hips—they are capable [of enchanting]. || KDd 3.30 ||

children.text: uditair anyapuṣṭānām ārutair me hṛtaṃ manaḥ /
children.translated_text: By the risen cries of cuckoos nurtured by others, my heart is stolen;

children.text: uditair api te dūti mārutair api dakṣiṇaiḥ // KDd_3.31 //
children.translated_text: by the risen southern breezes as well, O messenger. || KDd 3.31 ||

children.text: surājitahriyo yūnāṃ tanum adhyāsate striyaḥ /
children.translated_text: Women, whose modesty has been well-conquered, mount the bodies of young men—

children.text: tanumadhyāḥ kṣaratsvedasurājitamukhendavaḥ // KDd_3.32 //
children.translated_text: slender-waisted, with moon-like faces resplendent with flowing perspiration. || KDd 3.32 ||

children.text: iti vyapetayamakaprabhedo 'py eṣa darśitaḥ /
children.translated_text: Thus the variety of disjoint <s>yamaka</s> has also been shown;

children.text: avyapetavyapetātmā vikalpo 'py asti tadyathā // KDd_3.33 //
children.translated_text: there is also a variety that combines both non-disjoint and disjoint—that is as follows: || KDd 3.33 ||

children.text: sālaṃ sālambakalikāsālaṃ sālaṃ na vīkṣitum /
children.translated_text: She cannot bear to look at the <s>śāla</s> tree with its hanging flower-buds, nor the <s>śāla</s> grove;

children.text: nālīn ālīnabakulān ālī nālīkinīr api // KDd_3.34 //
children.translated_text: nor the rows of trees with bees hiding among <s>bakula</s> blossoms, nor the lotus-pools. || KDd 3.34 ||

children.text: kālaṃ kālam anālakṣyatāratārakam īkṣitum /
children.translated_text: Time after time, gazing at the imperceptible stars in the sky,

children.text: tāratāramyarasitaṃ kālaṃ kālamahāghanam // KDd_3.35 //
children.translated_text: resounding with melodious cries, the dark time of the great monsoon cloud [arrives]. || KDd 3.35 ||

children.text: yāma yāmatrayādhīnāyāmayā maraṇaṃ niśā /
children.translated_text: O watch of the night! The night governed by three watches, with its unceasing duration, is death;

children.text: yām ayām adhiyāsvārtyā yā mayā mathitaiva sā // KDd_3.36 //
children.translated_text: that night which must be endured in distress—that has been churned by me alone. || KDd 3.36 ||

children.text: ity ādipādayamakavikalpasyedṛśī gatiḥ /
children.translated_text: Thus is the course of the variety of <s>yamaka</s> at the beginning of the verse-quarter.

children.text: evam eva vikalpyāni yamakānītarāṇy api // KDd_3.37 //
children.translated_text: In the same way, the other <s>yamakas</s> are also to be elaborated. || KDd 3.37 ||

children.text: na prapañcabhayād bhedāḥ kārtsnyenākhyātum īpsitāḥ /
children.translated_text: Due to fear of prolixity, it is not desired to enumerate all the varieties completely;

children.text: duṣkarābhimatā eva darśyante tatra ke cana // KDd_3.38 //
children.translated_text: only some that are considered difficult are shown here. || KDd 3.38 ||

children.text: sthirāyate yatendriyo na hīyate yater bhavān /
children.translated_text: When you strive, the senses become firm; when you strive, you are not diminished;

children.text: amāyateyate 'py abhūt sukhāya te 'yate kṣayam // KDd_3.39 //
children.translated_text: when you go, even what was immeasurable comes about for your happiness; ruin departs. || KDd 3.39 ||

children.text: sabhāsu rājann asurāhatair mukhair mahīsurāṇāṃ vasurājitaiḥ stutāḥ /
children.translated_text: In assemblies, O king, praised by the faces of brahmins unhurt by demons, radiant with wealth,

children.text: na bhāsurā yānti surān na te guṇāḥ prajāsu rāgātmasu rāśitāṃ gatāḥ // KDd_3.40 //
children.translated_text: your shining qualities surpass the gods; among the passionately devoted subjects, they have reached abundance. || KDd 3.40 ||

children.text: tava priyā saccaritāpramatta yā vibhūṣaṇaṃ dhāryam ihāṃśumat tayā /
children.translated_text: Your beloved, of good conduct and vigilance—the ornament to be worn here, lustrous, by her—

children.text: ratotsavāmodaviśeṣamattayā na me phalaṃ kiṃ cana kāntimattayā // KDd_3.41 //
children.translated_text: intoxicated by the special fragrance of the festival of love—no fruit comes to me from her radiance. || KDd 3.41 ||

children.text: bhavādṛśā nātha na jānate nate rasaṃ viruddhe khalu sannatenate /
children.translated_text: O lord, those like you do not know the sentiment in one who has bowed; indeed, in opposition, those who bow are destroyed.

children.text: ya eva dīnāḥ śirasā natena te caranty alaṃ dainyarasena tena te // KDd_3.42 //
children.translated_text: Those very wretched ones who bow with their heads—those of yours move about steeped in the sentiment of wretchedness. || KDd 3.42 ||

children.text: līlāsmitena śucinā mṛdunoditena vyālokitena laghunā guruṇā gatena /
children.translated_text: With a playful, pure, soft-spoken smile; with a light yet profound glance;

children.text: vyājṛmbhitena jaghanena ca darśitena sā hanti tena galitaṃ mama jīvitena // KDd_3.43 //
children.translated_text: with a displayed, expanded hip—she destroys with that my departing life. || KDd 3.43 ||

children.text: śrīmān amān amaravartmasamānamānam ātmānam ānatajagatprathamānamānam /
children.translated_text: The glorious one, without pride, who brought to proper honor the self honored as the foremost of the bowing world, equal to the path of the gods—

children.text: bhūmānam ānayata yaḥ sthitimān amāna nāmānam ānama tam apratimānamānam // KDd_3.44 //
children.translated_text: I bow to him of incomparable honor, the steadfast one of immeasurable glory and boundless dignity. || KDd 3.44 ||

children.text: sārayantam urasā ramayantī sārabhūtamurusāradharā tam /
children.translated_text: Pressing him with her chest, delighting him, she of essential substance, bearing great essence—

children.text: sārasānukṛtasārasakāñciḥ sā rasāyanam asāram avaiti // KDd_3.45 //
children.translated_text: with a girdle imitating the cry of cranes, she considers the elixir of love to be without essence. || KDd 3.45 ||

children.text: nayānayālocanayānayānayān ayānayāndhān vinayānayāyate /
children.translated_text: He who by policy examines policies and non-policies, who blinds the unwise by discipline—

children.text: na yān ayāsīr jinayānayā nayān ayānayās tāñ janayānayāśritān // KDd_3.46 //
children.translated_text: those whom you did not approach through the conqueror's policy, those resorted to non-policy—he brings them forth. || KDd 3.46 ||

children.text: raveṇa bhaumo dhvajavartivīraver aveji saṃyaty atulāstragaurave /
children.translated_text: <s>Bhauma</s> (son of Earth), by the battle-cry, the hero on the banner, was shaken in the encounter of incomparable weapon-might;

children.text: raver ivograsya puro harer aver aveta tulyaṃ ripum asya bhairave // KDd_3.47 //
children.translated_text: before the fierce one, like the sun before <s>Hari</s>, his enemy fled in terror. || KDd 3.47 ||

children.text: mayāmayālambyakalāmayāmayām ayām ayātavyavirāmayāmayā /
children.translated_text: By me, clinging to the illusory art, this night of unceasing illness—

children.text: mayāmayārtiṃ niśayāmayāmayā mayāmayāmūṃ karuṇāmayāmayā // KDd_3.48 //
children.translated_text: by me, the distress of disease in the night of illness, by me, compassionate yet full of illness. || KDd 3.48 ||

children.text: matāṃ dhunānāramatām akāmatām atāpalabdhāgrimatānulomatā /
children.translated_text: Shaking off the honored state, dispassion, desirelessness—the progressive state obtained through austerity;

children.text: matāv ayaty uttamatāvilomatām atāmyatas te samatā na vāmatā // KDd_3.49 //
children.translated_text: when opinion approaches the regressive state of excellence, for you who are untiring, there is equanimity, not perversity. || KDd 3.49 ||

children.text: kālakālagalakālakālamukhakālakāla kālakālapanakālakālaghanakāla kāla /
children.translated_text: O <s>Kāla</s> (Time/Death), O Dark-throated, O Death-faced Death of Death, O drinker of the poison of Time, O dense dark <s>Kāla</s>!

children.text: kālakālasi takā lakā lalanikālakālakālakālagatu kālakālakalikālakāla // KDd_3.50 //
children.translated_text: O <s>Kāla</s>, you who are the Death of Death, the playful one of the ages, may the bud of the Death of Death reach the <s>Kāla</s> of <s>Kāla</s>! || KDd 3.50 ||

children.text: saṃdaṣṭayamakasthānam antādī pādayor dvayoḥ /
children.translated_text: The <s>saṃdaṣṭa yamaka</s> (interlocking repetition), occurring at the end and beginning of two verse-quarters—

children.text: uktāntargatam apy etat svātantryeṇādya kīrtyate // KDd_3.51 //
children.translated_text: though included among those already stated, is now described independently. || KDd 3.51 ||

children.text: upoḍharāgāpy abalā madena sā madenasā manyurasena yojitā /
children.translated_text: Although bearing love, that weak woman, joined by <s>Madana</s> with the sentiment of anger—

children.text: na yojitātmānam anaṅgatāpitāṃ gatāpi tāpāya mamāsa neyate // KDd_3.52 //
children.translated_text: she, joined to love, tormented by <s>Anaṅga</s> (Cupid), having gone, does not bring herself to cause suffering to me. || KDd 3.52 ||

children.text: ardhābhyāsaḥ samudgaḥ syāt tasya bhedās trayo matāḥ /
children.translated_text: The repetition of half a verse is called <s>samudga</s> (casket); three varieties of it are recognized.

children.text: pādābhyāso 'py anekātmā vyajyate sa nidarśanaiḥ // KDd_3.53 //
children.translated_text: The repetition of a quarter also has many forms; it is illustrated by examples. || KDd 3.53 ||

children.text: nāsthe yaḥ sa tvayā varjyaḥ paramāyatamānayā /
children.translated_text: He who does not care is to be avoided by you of supreme extended pride;

children.text: nā stheyaḥsattvayāvarjyaḥ param āyatamānayā // KDd_3.54 //
children.translated_text: he should not be relied upon—he is to be avoided with supreme extended humility by one of good character. || KDd 3.54 ||

children.text: narā jitā mānanayāsam etya na rājitā mānanayā sametya /
children.translated_text: Men are conquered when they approach with the policy of wounded pride; they are not adorned when they come together with the policy of pride.

children.text: vināśitā vaibhavatāpanena vināśitā vai bhavatāpanena // KDd_3.55 //
children.translated_text: [She was] destroyed by the heat of [his] splendor; [she was] indeed destroyed, O lord, by the heat [of separation]. // KDd 3.55 //

children.text: kalāpināṃ cārutayopayanti vṛndāni lāpoḍhaghanāgamānām /
children.translated_text: Flocks of peacocks, beautiful, approach, bearing the advent of the dense [rain-]clouds;

children.text: vṛndānilāpoḍhaghanāgamānāṃ kalāpināṃ cārutayo 'payanti // KDd_3.56 //
children.translated_text: the beauties of peacocks bearing [their tails] depart [at the approach] of flocks carrying the dense [rain-]clouds. // KDd 3.56 //

children.text: naman dayāvarjitamānasātmayā na mandayāvarjitamānasātmayā /
children.translated_text: By me, whose mind was won over by compassion, bowing,

children.text: urasy upāstīrṇapayodharadvayaṃ mayā samāliṅgyata jīviteśvaraḥ // KDd_3.57 //
children.translated_text: with her pair of breasts pressed against [his] chest, the lord of my life was embraced. // KDd 3.57 //

children.text: sabhā surāṇām abalā vibhūṣitā guṇais tavārohi mṛṇālanirmalaiḥ /
children.translated_text: The assembly of the gods, adorned by women, radiant with your virtues, pure as lotus-stalks —

children.text: sa bhāsurāṇām abalā vibhūṣitā vihārayan nirviśa saṃpadaḥ purām // KDd_3.58 //
children.translated_text: enjoy without anxiety the splendor of the city, adorned by women resplendent [with ornaments]. // KDd 3.58 //

children.text: kalaṃ kam uktaṃ tanumaddhyanāmikā stanadvayī ca tvadṛte na hanty ataḥ /
children.translated_text: What sweet word has the slender-named [ring finger] uttered? The pair of breasts — apart from you — does not kill; therefore

children.text: na yāti bhūtaṃ gaṇane bhavanmukhe kalaṅkamuktaṃ tanumad dhy anāmikā // KDd_3.59 //
children.translated_text: nothing real enters into reckoning before your face; the ring finger, slender-bodied and freed from blemish. // KDd 3.59 //

children.text: yaśaś ca te dikṣu rajaś ca sainikā vitanvate 'jopama daṃśitā yudhā /
children.translated_text: Your fame in the quarters, and the dust [raised by] soldiers — [both] are spread by warriors armored [like] <s>Aja</s> in battle;

children.text: vitanv atejo 'pamadaṃ śitāyudhā dviṣāṃ ca kurvanti kulaṃ tarasvinaḥ // KDd_3.60 //
children.translated_text: the sharp-weaponed [warriors] also spread the splendor that crushes the pride [of foes], and make the families of enemies [tremble], being vigorous. // KDd 3.60 //

children.text: bibharti bhūmer valayaṃ bhujena te bhujaṅgamo 'mā smarato mad añcitam /
children.translated_text: Your arm bears the girdle of the earth; the serpent [<s>Śeṣa</s>] [also bears it], remembering me, adorned [by you];

children.text: śṛṇūktam ekaṃ svam avetya bhūdharaṃ bhujaṃ gamo mā sma rato madaṃ citam // KDd_3.61 //
children.translated_text: hear this one [instruction]: knowing your own mountain-bearing [arm], O arm, do not indulge in pride, [even in] thought! // KDd 3.61 //

children.text: smarānalo mānavivardhito yaḥ sa nirvṛtiṃ te kim apākaroti /
children.translated_text: The fire of love, increased by pride — does it not take away your pleasure?

children.text: samantatas tāmarasekṣaṇe na samaṃ tatas tām arase kṣaṇena // KDd_3.62 //
children.translated_text: On all sides, O lotus-eyed one, do not taste that [pleasure] equally even for a moment! // KDd 3.62 //

children.text: prabhāvato nāmana vāsavasya prabhāvato 'nāma navāsavasya /
children.translated_text: Through the might of <s>Vāsava</s> (<s>Indra</s>), or through the might indeed of the new <s>Vāsava</s> [i.e., you],

children.text: prabhāv ato nāma na vā savasya vicchittir āsīt tvayi piṣṭapasya // KDd_3.63 //
children.translated_text: or through the might of one named 'not <s>Vāsava</s>' — was there [ever] a defeat for the crusher of <s>Piṣṭapa</s>? // KDd 3.63 //

children.text: paraṃ parāyā balavā raṇānāṃ dhūlīsthalīr vyoma vidhāya rundhan /
children.translated_text: The supreme, mighty [king] of battles, of the vanguard of the enemy, making dust-clouds [that] block the sky,

children.text: paraṃ parāyā balavāraṇānāṃ paramparāyā balavāraṇānām // KDd_3.64 //
children.translated_text: [destroys] the column of the enemy's strongest elephants, the line of the enemy's mightiest elephants. // KDd 3.64 //

children.text: na śraddadhe vācam alajja mithyā bhavadvidhānām asamāhitānām /
children.translated_text: I do not believe the false words of shameless ones like you, whose minds are unsteady —

children.text: bhavadvidhānām asamāhitānāṃ bhavadvidhānām asamāhitānām // KDd_3.65 //
children.translated_text: [words] of those like you who are unsteady, of those like you who are unsteady. // KDd 3.65 //

children.text: sannāhitomānamarājasena sannā hitomānamarājasena /
children.translated_text: [He who is] armored, [his] pride produced by a king; [he who is] armored, [his] pride produced by a king;

children.text: sann āhito mānam arājasena saṃnāhito mānama rājase na // KDd_3.66 //
children.translated_text: [he who is] properly placed, [his] pride [coming from] a non-royal [source]; [he who is] armored — no pride in a kingly [manner]. // KDd 3.66 //

children.text: sakṛd dvis triś ca yo 'bhyāsaḥ pādasyaivaṃ pradarśitaḥ /
children.translated_text: The repetition of a quarter once, twice, or thrice has thus been demonstrated;

children.text: ślokadvayaṃ tu yuktārthaṃ ślokābhyāsaḥ smṛto yathā // KDd_3.67 //
children.translated_text: but when two verses form a connected meaning, it is known as verse-repetition (<s>ślokābhyāsa</s>), as follows: // KDd 3.67 //

children.text: vināyakena bhavatā vṛttopacitabāhunā /
children.translated_text: By you, the remover [of obstacles], with arms bulging from deeds,

children.text: svamitroddhāriṇābhītā pṛthvīyam atulāśritā // KDd_3.68 //
children.translated_text: the rescuer of your own friends — this earth, fearlessly, has sought [your] incomparable [protection]. // KDd 3.68 //

children.text: vināyakena bhavatā vṛttopacitabāhunā /
children.translated_text: By you, <s>Vināyaka</s> [<s>Gaṇeśa</s>], with arms bulging from deeds,

children.text: svamitroddhāriṇābhītā pṛthvī yamatulāśritā // KDd_3.69 //
children.translated_text: the rescuer of his own friend — this earth has taken refuge [with one] equal to <s>Yama</s>, fearlessly. // KDd 3.69 //

children.text: ekākāracatuṣpādaṃ tan mahāyamakāhvayam /
children.translated_text: That which has four quarters of identical form is called <s>mahāyamaka</s> (great <s>yamaka</s>);

children.text: tasyāpi dṛśyate 'bhyāsaḥ sā parā yamakakriyā // KDd_3.70 //
children.translated_text: the repetition of that too is observed — that is the supreme art of <s>yamaka</s>. // KDd 3.70 //

children.text: samānayāsamānayā samānayā sa mānayā /
children.translated_text: Bring them, O do not bring, O bring, O honor [them]!

children.text: samānayāsamāna yā samānayāsamānayā // KDd_3.71 //
children.translated_text: O bring, O one not equal, O do not bring, O bring! // KDd 3.71 //

children.text: dharādharākāradharā dharābhujāṃ bhujā mahīṃ pātum ahīnavikramāḥ /
children.translated_text: The arms of kings, bearing the earth in the form of [its] mountains, [arms that are] bearers of the earth,

children.text: kramāt sahante sahasā hatārayo rayoddhurā mānadhurāvalambinaḥ // KDd_3.72 //
children.translated_text: of no mean valor, to protect the earth — they endure gradually, having struck enemies by force, [those arms] resting on the yoke of valor, charioteers of dust. // KDd 3.72 //

children.text: āvṛttiḥ prātilomyena pādārdhaślokagocarā /
children.translated_text: The reversal of a half-quarter or full verse [when read backwards] —

children.text: yamakaṃ pratilomatvāt pratilomam iti smṛtam // KDd_3.73 //
children.translated_text: that <s>yamaka</s> is called <s>pratiloma</s> (reverse) due to its being [read] in reverse order. // KDd 3.73 //

children.text: yāmatāśa kṛtāyāsā sā yātā kṛśatā mayā /
children.translated_text: Gone into the night, she who made exertions — that thinness has come to me;

children.text: ramaṇārakatā te 'stu stutetākaraṇāmara // KDd_3.74 //
children.translated_text: may the non-return to the beloved be yours! [Reversed:] O immortal one of undimished deeds, may you be praised! // KDd 3.74 //

children.text: nādino 'madanā dhīḥ svā na me kā cana kāmitā /
children.translated_text: The intellect of the thundering [ones] is one's own, not [that of the] lustful; I have no desire whatsoever;

children.text: tāmikā na ca kāmena svādhīnā damanodinā // KDd_3.75 //
children.translated_text: [Reversed:] My dark-complexioned [beloved] is not [moved] by desire; she is independent, [like one] who subdues what shines. // KDd 3.75 //

children.text: yā na mānayamārāvikaśonānajanāsanā /
children.translated_text: She who does not honor, who is the abode of the enemy <s>Māra's</s> radiance, whose seat is the people —

children.text: yām udāraśatādhīnām āyām āyam anādi sā // KDd_3.76 //
children.translated_text: she who is subject to a hundred noble [qualities], whose extent is measureless and beginningless — // KDd 3.76 //

children.text: sā dināmayam āyāmā nādhītā śaradāmuyā /
children.translated_text: [Reversed:] She, the poor one, of [such] an extent — she who has not been studied [even in] autumn by her —

children.text: nāsanājananā śokavirāmāya na mānayā // KDd_3.77 //
children.translated_text: she whose seat is not the people, radiant as <s>Māra's</s> enemy, she does not honor. // KDd 3.77 //

children.text: varṇānām ekarūpatvaṃ yady ekāntaram ardhayoḥ /
children.translated_text: When the identity of syllables [occurs] at every other half-verse,

children.text: gomūtriketi tat prāhur duṣkaraṃ tadvido yathā // KDd_3.78 //
children.translated_text: those expert in it call that <s>gomūtrikā</s> (cow-urine pattern), as follows: // KDd 3.78 //

children.text: madano madirākṣīṇām apāṅgāstro jayed ayam /
children.translated_text: <s>Madana</s> (Love) would conquer with the weapon of side-glances of intoxicated-eyed women;

children.text: madeno yadi tat kṣīṇam anaṅgāyāñjaliṃ dadhe // KDd_3.79 //
children.translated_text: if by <s>Madana</s> that [weapon] is diminished, [then] I offer salutation to <s>Anaṅga</s> (the Bodiless One). // KDd 3.79 //

children.text: āhur ardhabhramaṃ nāma ślokārdhabhramaṇaṃ yadi /
children.translated_text: They call it <s>ardhabhrama</s> (half-revolution) when there is the rotation of half a verse;

children.text: tad iṣṭaṃ sarvatobhadraṃ bhramaṇaṃ yadi sarvataḥ // KDd_3.80 //
children.translated_text: it is called <s>sarvatobhadra</s> (auspicious in all directions) when there is rotation in all directions. // KDd 3.80 //

children.text: manobhava tavānīkaṃ nodayāya na māninī /
children.translated_text: O <s>Manobhava</s> (Love)! Do not deploy your army; the proud woman [will not yield];

children.text: bhayād ameyāmā mā vā vayam enomayā nata // KDd_3.81 //
children.translated_text: [Reversed:] Out of fear, O measureless one — or rather, we [bow to] you, sinless one, with salutations. // KDd 3.81 //

children.text: sāmāyāmā mā yā māsā mārānāyāyānā rāmā /
children.translated_text: [A <s>sarvatobhadra</s> verse, identical when read forward and backward:] [The verse plays on repetitive syllables <s>mā</s>, <s>yā</s>, <s>sā</s>, <s>rā</s>, <s>nā</s> in palindromic patterns]

children.text: yānāvārārāvānāyā māyārāmā mārāyāmā // KDd_3.82 //
children.translated_text: [continuing the palindromic <s>sarvatobhadra</s> pattern with <s>yā</s>, <s>nā</s>, <s>vā</s>, <s>rā</s>, <s>mā</s>] // KDd 3.82 //

children.text: yaḥ svarasthānavarṇānāṃ niyamo duṣkareṣv asau /
children.translated_text: The constraint [of specific arrangement] of vowels, positions, and consonants in the difficult [compositions] —

children.text: iṣṭaś catuḥprabhṛty eṣa darśyate sukaraḥ paraḥ // KDd_3.83 //
children.translated_text: this is desired from the fourth [type] onward; the other [simpler type] is shown [to be] easy. // KDd 3.83 //

children.text: āmnāyānām āhāntyā vāg ītīr gītīr bhītīḥ prītīḥ /
children.translated_text: [Example with restricted vowels:] Of the scriptures, the final speech — these songs, these fears, these pleasures;

children.text: bhogo rogo modo moho dheye dhecche deśe kṣeme // KDd_3.84 //
children.translated_text: enjoyment, disease, delight, delusion; in what is to be contemplated, in desire, in the land, in prosperity. // KDd 3.84 //

children.text: kṣitivijitisthitivihitivrataratayaḥ paragatayaḥ /
children.translated_text: [Example with restricted consonants:] Conquering the earth, establishing stability, performing rites, delighting in vows, [attaining] the highest destinations —

children.text: uru rurudhur guru dudhuvur yudhi kuravaḥ svam arikulam // KDd_3.85 //
children.translated_text: the <s>Kurus</s> greatly held back and greatly shook in battle their own enemy-host. // KDd 3.85 //

children.text: śrīdīptī hrīkīrtī dhīnītī gīḥprītī /
children.translated_text: [Example with paired long vowels:] Prosperity and splendor, modesty and fame, wisdom and policy, speech and love —

children.text: edhete dve dve te ye neme deveśe // KDd_3.86 //
children.translated_text: these two by two flourish in him who is the lord of gods. // KDd 3.86 //

children.text: sāmāyāmā mā yā māsā mārānāyāyānā rāmā /
children.translated_text: [Repeated palindromic <s>sarvatobhadra</s> example:] [Same syllabic palindrome as verses 162-163]

children.text: yānāvārārāvānāyā māyārāmā mārāyāmā // KDd_3.87 //
children.translated_text: [continuing palindromic pattern] // KDd 3.87 //

children.text: nayanānandajanane nakṣatragaṇaśālini /
children.translated_text: O you who produce delight in the eyes, O you adorned with hosts of stars!

children.text: aghane gagane dṛṣṭir aṅgane dīyatāṃ sakṛt // KDd_3.88 //
children.translated_text: O cloudless sky, let the gaze be cast upon [you] even once! // KDd 3.88 //

children.text: alinīlālakalataṃ kaṃ na hanti ghanastani /
children.translated_text: [Your] face with bee-dark curling locks — whom does it not slay, O full-breasted one?

children.text: ānanaṃ nalinacchāyanayanaṃ śaśikānti te // KDd_3.89 //
children.translated_text: Your face, with lotus-like shadow-eyes, shining like the moon! // KDd 3.89 //

children.text: anaṅgalaṅghanālagnanānātaṅkā sadaṅganā /
children.translated_text: O woman, free from anxiety, clinging to the transgression of <s>Anaṅga</s> (Love)!

children.text: sadānagha sadānanda natāṅgāsaṅgasaṃgata // KDd_3.90 //
children.translated_text: O ever-sinless, ever-blissful one, attained through the company of a bowed-limbed [lover]! // KDd 3.90 //

children.text: agā gāṃ gāṅgakākākagāhakāghakakākahā /
children.translated_text: [Verse composed with only guttural consonants:] She went to the earth; the killer of crows who dives into the <s>Gaṅgā's</s> waters, the destroyer of sins, the crow-killer —

children.text: ahāhāṅga khagāṅkāgakaṅkāgakhagakākaka // KDd_3.91 //
children.translated_text: Alas, alas! O bird-marked one, you who grasp the mark of birds, O kite-grasping, bird-[-like], crow-[like one]! // KDd 3.91 //

children.text: re re rorūrurūrorugāgogo 'gāṅgago 'gaguḥ /
children.translated_text: [Verse with restricted consonants:] O, O, the roaring heroes roaring heroically! The go-[people], the go-[folk], the <s>Gaṅgā</s>-goers who went without going!

children.text: kiṃ kekākākukaḥ kāko mā mā mām āma māmama // KDd_3.92 //
children.translated_text: What! Is the screeching crow a crow? No, no, do not [harm] me! O afflicted one, O my mother! // KDd 3.92 //

children.text: devānāṃ nandano devo nodano vedanindinaḥ /
children.translated_text: [Verse with dental consonants:] The god <s>Nandana</s> (<s>Indra</s>) of the gods, the impeller, the reviler of the <s>Veda</s>-revilers,

children.text: divaṃ dudāva nādena dāne dānavanandinaḥ // KDd_3.93 //
children.translated_text: with his sound he split the sky, [overcoming] the joy of the <s>Dānavas</s> (demons) in their generosity. // KDd 3.93 //

children.text: sūriḥ surāsurāsārisāraḥ sārāsisārasāḥ /
children.translated_text: [Verse with sibilants and 'r':] The wise one, the essence of gods and demons' enemy, the essence of the lotus-pond swan;

children.text: sasāra sarasīḥ sīrī sasūruḥ sa surārasī // KDd_3.94 //
children.translated_text: he traversed the lakes; the plowman, with the enemy of the gods' foe. // KDd 3.94 //

children.text: nūnaṃ nunnāni nānena nānanenānanāni naḥ /
children.translated_text: [Verse with nasals:] Surely, our faces were beaten again and again by that,

children.text: nānenā nanu nānūnenainenānān ino ninīḥ // KDd_3.95 //
children.translated_text: not by a lesser one — by that sinful one, the debtor-[destroyer] led the indebted ones. // KDd 3.95 //

children.text: iti duṣkaramārgo 'pi kiṃcidādarśitakramaḥ /
children.translated_text: Thus, even the path of the difficult [compositions] has been shown in some measure;

children.text: prahelikāprakārāṇāṃ punar uddiśyate gatiḥ // KDd_3.96 //
children.translated_text: now the course of the types of riddles (<s>prahelikā</s>) will be indicated. // KDd 3.96 //

children.text: krīḍāgoṣṭhīvinodeṣu tajjñair ākīrṇamantraṇe /
children.translated_text: In playful gatherings, in amusements, in councils filled with experts,

children.text: paravyāmohane cāpi sopayogāḥ prahelikāḥ // KDd_3.97 //
children.translated_text: and in bewildering others — riddles (<s>prahelikā</s>) have their use. // KDd 3.97 //

children.text: āhuḥ samāgatāṃ nāma gūḍhārthāṃ padasaṃdhinā /
children.translated_text: They call <s>samāgatā</s> (the 'encountered') a riddle with hidden meaning through word-junction (<s>padasandhi</s>),

children.text: vañcitānyatra rūḍhena yatra śabdena vañcanā // KDd_3.98 //
children.translated_text: where the deception is through a word well-established [in another meaning]. // KDd 3.98 //

children.text: vyutkrāntātivyavahitaprayogān mohakāriṇī /
children.translated_text: The <s>pramuṣitā</s> (the 'robbed'), which causes bewilderment through transposed, excessive, or widely separated usage,

children.text: sā syāt pramuṣitā yasyā durbodhārthā padāvalī // KDd_3.99 //
children.translated_text: is that [riddle] whose sequence of words has a meaning difficult to comprehend. // KDd 3.99 //

children.text: samānarūpā gauṇārthāropitair grathitā padaiḥ /
children.translated_text: The <s>samānarūpā</s> (the 'similarly formed') is composed with words loaded with secondary meanings,

children.text: paruṣā lakṣaṇāstitvamātravyutpāditaśrutiḥ // KDd_3.100 //
children.translated_text: [and] the <s>paruṣā</s> (the 'harsh') has its expression derived merely from the presence of a characteristic. // KDd 3.100 //

children.text: saṃkhyātā nāma saṃkhyānaṃ yatra vyāmohakāraṇam /
children.translated_text: The one called <s>saṃkhyātā</s> (the 'counted') is that in which enumeration is the cause of bewilderment;

children.text: anyathā bhāsate yatra vākyārthaḥ sā prakalpitā // KDd_3.101 //
children.translated_text: the <s>prakalpitā</s> (the 'contrived') is that in which the sentence-meaning appears otherwise [than intended]. // KDd 3.101 //

children.text: sā nāmāntaritā yasyā nāmni nānārthakalpanā /
children.translated_text: The one called <s>antaritā</s> (the 'concealed') is that in which there is the construction of multiple meanings in a name;

children.text: nibhṛtā nibhṛtānyārthā tulyadharmaspṛśā girā // KDd_3.102 //
children.translated_text: the <s>nibhṛtā</s> (the 'secret') has a hidden alternative meaning through words touching a common property. // KDd 3.102 //

children.text: samānaśabdopanyastaśabdaparyāyasādhitā /
children.translated_text: The <s>saṃmūḍhā</s> (the 'confused') is that which, though its meaning is directly stated, is accomplished

children.text: saṃmūḍhā nāma yā sākṣān nirdiṣṭārthāpi mūḍhaye // KDd_3.103 //
children.translated_text: through a synonym presented by a homonymous word — [it serves] for bewilderment. // KDd 3.103 //

children.text: yogamālātmakaṃ nāma yasyāḥ sā pārihārikī /
children.translated_text: That whose nature is a series of puzzles (<s>yogamālā</s>) is the <s>pārihārikī</s>;

children.text: ekacchannāśritaṃ vyajya yasyām āśrayagopanam // KDd_3.104 //
children.translated_text: the <s>ekacchannā</s> (the 'singly concealed') is that in which one [element] is concealed while being revealed by another. // KDd 3.104 //

children.text: sā bhaved ubhayacchannā yasyām ubhayagopanam /
children.translated_text: The <s>ubhayacchannā</s> (the 'doubly concealed') is that in which both [elements] are concealed;

children.text: saṃkīrṇā nāma sā yasyā nānālakṣaṇasaṃkaraḥ // KDd_3.105 //
children.translated_text: the <s>saṃkīrṇā</s> (the 'mixed') is that in which there is a mixture of various characteristics. // KDd 3.105 //

children.text: etāḥ ṣoḍaśa nirdiṣṭāḥ pūrvācāryaiḥ prahelikāḥ /
children.translated_text: These sixteen riddles have been declared by the earlier masters,

children.text: duṣṭaprahelikāś cānyās tair adhītāś caturdaśa // KDd_3.106 //
children.translated_text: and fourteen defective riddles (<s>duṣṭaprahelikā</s>) have also been studied by them. // KDd 3.106 //

children.text: doṣān aparisaṃkhyeyān manyamānā vayaṃ punaḥ /
children.translated_text: We, however, considering the faults to be innumerable,

children.text: sādhvīr evābhidhāsyāmas tā duṣṭā yās tv alakṣaṇāḥ // KDd_3.107 //
children.translated_text: shall describe only the good ones — those that lack characteristics are defective. // KDd 3.107 //

children.text: na may āgorasābhijñaṃ cetaḥ kasmāt prakupyasi /
children.translated_text: 'My heart is not acquainted with the taste of crime — why are you angry?

children.text: asthānaruditair ebhir alam ālohitekṣaṇe // KDd_3.108 //
children.translated_text: Enough of these tears shed without cause, O red-eyed one!' // KDd 3.108 //

children.text: kubjām āsevamānasya yathā te vardhate ratiḥ /
children.translated_text: 'As your passion increases by serving a hunchbacked woman,

children.text: naivaṃ nirviśato nārīr amarastrīviḍambinīḥ // KDd_3.109 //
children.translated_text: it does not so [increase] by enjoying women who rival celestial maidens.' // KDd 3.109 //

children.text: daṇḍe cumbati padminyā haṃsaḥ karkaśakaṇṭake /
children.translated_text: The swan kisses the stalk of the lotus, [though it is] rough with thorns;

children.text: mukhaṃ valgu ravaṃ kurvaṃs tuṇḍenāṅgāni ghaṭayan // KDd_3.110 //
children.translated_text: making a charming face, producing a sound, arranging its limbs with its beak. // KDd 3.110 //

children.text: khātayaḥ kani kāle te sphātayaḥ sphītavalgavaḥ /
children.translated_text: What are your excavations? At what time are your expansions, when [you are] full and pleasing?

children.text: candre sākṣādbhavanty atra tāyavo mama dhāriṇaḥ // KDd_3.111 //
children.translated_text: [Answer: the moon —] here, directly in the moon, my bearers become visible. // KDd 3.111 //

children.text: atrodyāne mayā dṛṣṭā vallarī pañcapallavā /
children.translated_text: In this garden, I saw a creeper with five leaves,

children.text: pallave pallave cārdrā yasyāḥ kusumamañjarī // KDd_3.112 //
children.translated_text: on each leaf of which was a moist cluster of flowers. // KDd 3.112 //

children.text: surāḥ surālaye svairaṃ bhramanti daśanārciṣā /
children.translated_text: The gods wander freely in the abode of the gods, with the radiance of their teeth;

children.text: majjanta iva mattās te saure sarasi saṃprati // KDd_3.113 //
children.translated_text: those intoxicated ones seem to be immersed now in the pool of the sun. // KDd 3.113 //

children.text: nāsikyamadhyā paritaś caturvarṇavibhūṣitā /
children.translated_text: Central in the nose, adorned all around with four castes —

children.text: asti kā cit purī yasyām aṣṭavarṇāhvayā nṛpāḥ // KDd_3.114 //
children.translated_text: there is a certain city in which there are kings with names of eight syllables. // KDd 3.114 //

children.text: girā skhalantyā namreṇa śirasā dīnayā dṛśā /
children.translated_text: With faltering speech, with bowed head, with a pitiful gaze,

children.text: tiṣṭhantam api sotkampaṃ vṛddhe māṃ nānukampase // KDd_3.115 //
children.translated_text: standing, yet trembling — O aged one, you do not show compassion to me! // KDd 3.115 //

children.text: ādau rājety adhīrākṣi pārthivaḥ ko 'pi gīyate /
children.translated_text: At first, 'king' is read, O unsteady-eyed one! Some ruler is being praised;

children.text: sa nātanaś ca naivāsau rājā nāpi sanātanaḥ // KDd_3.116 //
children.translated_text: but he is not an actor, nor is he a king, nor is he eternal. // KDd 3.116 //

children.text: hṛtadravyaṃ naraṃ tyaktvā dhanavantaṃ vrajanti kāḥ /
children.translated_text: Who are those women who abandon a man whose wealth has been stolen and go to the wealthy one?

children.text: nānābhaṅgiśatākṛṣṭalokā veśyā na durdharāḥ // KDd_3.117 //
children.translated_text: Courtesans, who attract people by hundreds of various wiles, are not hard to bear. // KDd 3.117 //

children.text: jitaprakṛṣṭakeśākhyo yas tavābhūmisāhvayaḥ /
children.translated_text: He who was named 'conqueror of distinguished hair' and was your 'not-earth-named' [companion] —

children.text: sa mām adya prabhūtotkaṃ karoti kalabhāṣiṇi // KDd_3.118 //
children.translated_text: he makes me today exceedingly longing, O sweet-voiced one! // KDd 3.118 //

children.text: śayanīye parāvṛtya śayitau kāminau ruṣā /
children.translated_text: Turning over on the bed, the two lovers lay in anger;

children.text: tathaiva śayitau rāgāt svairaṃ mukham acumbatām // KDd_3.119 //
children.translated_text: in just the same way they lay from passion, freely kissing each other's face. // KDd 3.119 //

children.text: vijitānnabhavadveṣigurupādahato janaḥ /
children.translated_text: People, struck by the feet of the revered teacher who is the foe of the conqueror of food [<s>Vijitānna</s>],

children.text: himāpahāmitradharair vyāptaṃ vyomābhinandati // KDd_3.120 //
children.translated_text: rejoice at the sky pervaded by those who remove cold, hostility, and darkness. // KDd 3.120 //

children.text: na spṛśaty āyudhaṃ jātu na strīṇāṃ stanamaṇḍalam /
children.translated_text: He never touches a weapon, nor the rounded breasts of women —

children.text: amanuṣyasya kasyāpi hasto 'yaṃ na kilāphalaḥ // KDd_3.121 //
children.translated_text: this hand of a certain non-human being is surely not fruitless. // KDd 3.121 //

children.text: kena kaḥ saha saṃbhūya sarvakāryeṣu saṃnidhim /
children.translated_text: Who, having come together with whom, [and] having obtained presence in all affairs,

children.text: labdhvā bhojanakāle tu yadi dṛṣṭo nirasyate // KDd_3.122 //
children.translated_text: is rejected when seen at mealtime? // KDd 3.122 //

children.text: sahayā sagajā senā sabhaṭeyaṃ na cej jitā /
children.translated_text: This army with horses, with elephants, with warriors — if it were not conquered,

children.text: amātṛko 'yaṃ mūḍhaḥ syād akṣarajñas tu naḥ sutaḥ // KDd_3.123 //
children.translated_text: this fool would be without a mother; but our son knows his letters. // KDd 3.123 //

children.text: sā nāmāntaritāmiśravañcitārūpayoginī /
children.translated_text: She — named otherwise, mixed-deceptive, a practitioner of false forms —

children.text: evam evetarāsām apy unneyaḥ saṃkarakramaḥ // KDd_3.124 //
children.translated_text: thus the method of mixing should be inferred for the remaining [types] as well. // KDd 3.124 //

children.text: iti prahelikāmārgo duṣkarātmāpi darśitaḥ /
children.translated_text: Thus the path of riddles (<s>prahelikā</s>) has been shown, though difficult in nature;

children.text: vidvatprayogato jñeyā mārgāḥ praśnottarādayaḥ // KDd_3.124*1 //
children.translated_text: the methods of questions-and-answers and the like are to be known from the practice of the learned. // KDd 3.124*1 //

children.text: viśadabuddhir anena suvartmanā sukaraduṣkaramārgam evaiti hi /
children.translated_text: One of clear intellect, by this good path, easily traverses even the difficult path;

children.text: na hi tadanyanaye 'pi kṛtaśramaḥ prabhur imaṃ nayam etum idaṃ vinā // KDd_3.124*2 //
children.translated_text: for one who has labored in another method is not capable of entering this method without this [instruction]. // KDd 3.124*2 //

children.text: kāvye doṣā guṇāś caiva vijñātavyā vicakṣaṇaiḥ /
children.translated_text: In poetry, both faults (<s>doṣa</s>) and virtues (<s>guṇa</s>) are to be recognized by the discerning;

children.text: doṣā vipattaye tatra guṇāḥ sampattaye yathā // KDd_3.124*3 //
children.translated_text: faults therein lead to failure, as virtues lead to success. // KDd 3.124*3 //

children.text: apārthaṃ vyartham ekārthaṃ sasaṃśayam apakramam /
children.translated_text: Meaningless (<s>apārtha</s>), contradictory (<s>vyartha</s>), redundant (<s>ekārtha</s>), ambiguous (<s>sasaṃśaya</s>), disordered (<s>apakrama</s>),

children.text: śabdahīnaṃ yatibhraṣṭaṃ bhinnavṛttaṃ visaṃdhikam // KDd_3.125 //
children.translated_text: deficient in words (<s>śabdahīna</s>), broken in caesura (<s>yatibhraṣṭa</s>), broken in meter (<s>bhinnavṛtta</s>), and defective in sandhi (<s>visaṃdhika</s>) —

children.text: deśakālakalālokanyāyāgamavirodhi ca /
children.translated_text: and contradicting the norms of place, time, arts, worldly practice, logic, and scripture —

children.text: iti doṣā daśaivaite varjyāḥ kāvyeṣu sūribhiḥ // KDd_3.126 //
children.translated_text: these ten alone are the faults to be avoided in poetry by the wise. // KDd 3.126 //

children.text: pratijñāhetudṛṣṭāntahānir doṣo na vety asau /
children.translated_text: Whether the absence of thesis, reason, and example is a fault or not —

children.text: vicāraḥ karkaśaprāyas tenālīḍhena kiṃ phalam // KDd_3.127 //
children.translated_text: that inquiry is mostly hairsplitting; what fruit is there from licking that? // KDd 3.127 //

children.text: samudāyārthaśūnyaṃ yat tad apārtham iheṣyate /
children.translated_text: What is devoid of a collective meaning is considered 'meaningless' (<s>apārtha</s>) here;

children.text: tan mattonmattabālānām ukter anyatra duṣyati // KDd_3.128 //
children.translated_text: that is faulty except in the speech of the intoxicated, the mad, or children. // KDd 3.128 //

children.text: samudraḥ pīyate so 'yam aham adya jarāturaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'This ocean is being drunk!' 'I am today afflicted with old age!'

children.text: amī garjanti jīmūtā harer airāvataḥ priyaḥ // KDd_3.129 //
children.translated_text: 'These clouds thunder!' '<s>Hari's</s> <s>Airāvata</s> is dear!' // KDd 3.129 //

children.text: idam asvasthacittānām abhidhānam aninditam /
children.translated_text: This is unobjectionable speech for those of disturbed mind;

children.text: itaratra kaviḥ ko vā prayuñjītaivamādikam // KDd_3.130 //
children.translated_text: elsewhere, what poet would employ such [expressions]? // KDd 3.130 //

children.text: ekavākye prabandhe vā pūrvāparaparāhatam /
children.translated_text: In a single sentence or in a composition, when the earlier and later [parts] are mutually contradictory,

children.text: viruddhārthatayā vyartham iti doṣeṣu paṭhyate // KDd_3.131 //
children.translated_text: that is 'contradictory' (<s>vyartha</s>) due to self-contradiction — this is listed among the faults. // KDd 3.131 //

children.text: jahi śatrukulaṃ kṛtsnaṃ jaya viśvaṃbharām imām /
children.translated_text: 'Destroy the entire enemy clan! Conquer this earth!

children.text: na ca te ko 'pi vidveṣṭā sarvabhūtānukampinaḥ // KDd_3.132 //
children.translated_text: And may you have no enemy, O compassionate one toward all beings!' // KDd 3.132 //

children.text: asti kā cid avasthā sā sābhiṣaṅgasya cetasaḥ /
children.translated_text: There is, however, a certain state of the biased mind

children.text: yasyāṃ bhaved abhimatā viruddhārthāpi bhāratī // KDd_3.133 //
children.translated_text: in which even contradictory speech (<s>viruddhārthā bhāratī</s>) might be welcome. // KDd 3.133 //

children.text: paradārābhilāṣo me katham āryasya yujyate /
children.translated_text: 'How can desire for another's wife befit a noble man?'

children.text: pibāmi taralaṃ tasyāḥ kadā nu daśanacchadam // KDd_3.134 //
children.translated_text: 'When indeed shall I drink the trembling lip of hers?' // KDd 3.134 //

children.text: aviśeṣeṇa pūrvoktaṃ yadi bhūyo 'pi kīrtyate /
children.translated_text: If what has been previously stated without distinction is stated again,

children.text: arthataḥ śabdato vāpi tad ekārthaṃ mataṃ yathā // KDd_3.135 //
children.translated_text: either in meaning or in words — that is considered 'redundant' (<s>ekārtha</s>), as for example: // KDd 3.135 //

children.text: utkām unmanayanty ete bālāṃ tadalakatviṣaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'These clouds, with lightning, deep with thunder, drive the longing maiden to distraction

children.text: ambhodharās taḍitvanto gambhīrāḥ stanayitnavaḥ // KDd_3.136 //
children.translated_text: with those flashes of their locks.' // KDd 3.136 //

children.text: anukampādyatiśayo yadi kaś cid vivakṣyate /
children.translated_text: But if some excess of compassion and the like is intended to be expressed,

children.text: na doṣaḥ punarukte 'pi pratyuteyam alaṃkṛtiḥ // KDd_3.137 //
children.translated_text: there is no fault even in repetition; on the contrary, this is an ornament (<s>alaṃkṛti</s>). // KDd 3.137 //

children.text: hanyate sā varārohā smareṇākāṇḍavairiṇā /
children.translated_text: 'She is slain, the fair-hipped one, by <s>Smara</s> (Love), the unprovoked enemy!

children.text: hanyate cārusarvāṅgī hanyate mañjubhāṣiṇī // KDd_3.138 //
children.translated_text: She is slain, the one beautiful in all limbs! She is slain, the sweet-voiced one!' // KDd 3.138 //

children.text: nirṇayārthaṃ prayuktāni saṃśayaṃ janayanti cet /
children.translated_text: If words employed to determine [a matter] give rise to doubt,

children.text: vacāṃsi doṣa evāsau sasaṃśaya iti smṛtaḥ // KDd_3.139 //
children.translated_text: that fault is indeed called 'ambiguous' (<s>sasaṃśaya</s>). // KDd 3.139 //

children.text: manorathapriyālokarasalolekṣaṇe sakhi /
children.translated_text: 'O friend, with eyes greedy for the delightful sight of a longed-for vision,

children.text: ārādvṛttir asau mātā na kṣamā draṣṭum īdṛśam // KDd_3.140 //
children.translated_text: that mother's conduct from afar is not able to behold such [a sight].' // KDd 3.140 //

children.text: īdṛśaṃ saṃśayāyaiva yadi jātu prayujyate /
children.translated_text: If such [ambiguity] is ever employed deliberately to create doubt,

children.text: syād alaṃkāra evāsau na doṣas tatra tadyathā // KDd_3.141 //
children.translated_text: then that is an ornament, not a fault — for instance: // KDd 3.141 //

children.text: paśyāmy anaṅgajātaṅkalaṅghitāṃ tām aninditām /
children.translated_text: 'I see that blameless one, overcome by the affliction born of <s>Anaṅga</s> (Love),

children.text: kālenaiva kaṭhoreṇa grastāṃ kiṃ nas tvadāśayā // KDd_3.142 //
children.translated_text: seized by cruel Time itself — or is it by your intention toward us?' // KDd 3.142 //

children.text: kāmārtā gharmataptā vety aniścayakaraṃ vacaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Is she love-sick or heat-struck?' — words that create uncertainty,

children.text: yuvānam ākulīkartum iti dūty āha narmaṇā // KDd_3.143 //
children.translated_text: thus the female messenger speaks playfully, to agitate the young man. // KDd 3.143 //

children.text: uddeśānuguṇo 'rthānām anudeśo na cet kṛtaḥ /
children.translated_text: If the elaboration of topics is not made in accordance with their initial enumeration,

children.text: apakramābhidhānaṃ taṃ doṣam ācakṣate yathā // KDd_3.144 //
children.translated_text: that fault is called 'disorder' (<s>apakrama</s>), as for example: // KDd 3.144 //

children.text: sthitinirmāṇasaṃhārahetavo jagatām ajāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'The unborn causes of the creation, maintenance, and destruction of the worlds —

children.text: śaṃbhunārāyaṇāmbhojayonayaḥ pālayantu vaḥ // KDd_3.145 //
children.translated_text: <s>Śambhu</s>, <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, and the lotus-born [<s>Brahmā</s>] — may they protect you!' // KDd 3.145 //

children.text: yatnasaṃbandhanirjñānahetuḥ ko 'pi kṛto yadi /
children.translated_text: But if some [special] reason for the connection or arrangement is produced with effort,

children.text: kramalaṅghanam apy āhur na doṣaṃ sūrayo yathā // KDd_3.146 //
children.translated_text: the wise say that even transgression of order is not a fault, as for example: // KDd 3.146 //

children.text: bandhutyāgas tanutyāgo deśatyāga iti triṣu /
children.translated_text: 'Abandoning kinsmen, abandoning the body, abandoning one's country — among these three,

children.text: ādyantāv āyatakleśau madhyamaḥ kṣaṇikajvaraḥ // KDd_3.147 //
children.translated_text: the first and last involve prolonged suffering; the middle one is a momentary fever.' // KDd 3.147 //

children.text: śabdahīnam anālakṣyalakṣyalakṣaṇapaddhatiḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Deficient in words' (<s>śabdahīna</s>) is a usage of words that follows a path of imperceptible characteristics,

children.text: padaprayogo 'śiṣṭeṣṭo na śiṣṭeṣṭo hi duṣyati // KDd_3.148 //
children.translated_text: not desired by the cultured; for what is desired by the cultured is not faulty. // KDd 3.148 //

children.text: avate bhavate bāhur mahīm arṇavaśakvarīm /
children.translated_text: 'Your arm protects (<s>avate bhavate bāhuḥ</s>) this earth girdled by oceans,

children.text: mahārājann ajijñāsau nāstīty āsāṃ girāṃ rasaḥ // KDd_3.149 //
children.translated_text: O great king!' — there is no desire to examine it, for such is not the essence of these words. // KDd 3.149 //

children.text: dakṣiṇādrer upasaran mārutaś cūtapādapān /
children.translated_text: 'The wind, approaching from the southern mountain,

children.text: kurute lalitādhūtapravālāṅkuraśobhinaḥ // KDd_3.150 //
children.translated_text: makes the mango trees beautiful with gracefully swaying young sprouts.' // KDd 3.150 //

children.text: ityādi śāstramāhātmyadarśanālasacetasām /
children.translated_text: Such [usages] and the like appear as errors to those of lazy mind who do not see the authority of grammar,

children.text: apabhāṣaṇavad bhāti na ca saubhāgyam ujjhati // KDd_3.151 //
children.translated_text: but they do not abandon their beauty. // KDd 3.151 //

children.text: ślokeṣu niyatasthānaṃ padacchedaṃ yatiṃ viduḥ /
children.translated_text: In verses, the regulated caesura at a fixed place, the word-break, is known as <s>yati</s> (caesura);

children.text: tadapetaṃ yatibhraṣṭaṃ śravaṇodvejanaṃ yathā // KDd_3.152 //
children.translated_text: that which is devoid of it is 'broken in caesura' (<s>yatibhraṣṭa</s>), offensive to the ear, as for example: // KDd 3.152 //

children.text: strīṇāṃ saṃgītividhim ayam ādityavaṃśyo narendraḥ paśyaty akliṣṭarasam iha śiṣṭair ametyādi duṣṭam /
children.translated_text: 'This king of the solar dynasty watches the art of music of women with effortless delight' — here 'with the cultured ones not coming' and so forth is faulty.

children.text: kāryākāryāṇy ayam avikalāny āgamenaiva paśyan vaśyām urvīṃ vahati nṛpa ity asti caivaṃ prayogaḥ // KDd_3.153 //
children.translated_text: 'This king, seeing all duties and non-duties by scripture alone, bears the obedient earth' — there is indeed such usage. // KDd 3.153 //

children.text: lupte padānte śiṣṭasya padatvaṃ niścitaṃ yathā /
children.translated_text: Just as when the end of a word is elided, the remaining form is still recognized as a word,

children.text: tathā saṃdhivikārāntaṃ padam eveti varṇyate // KDd_3.154 //
children.translated_text: so too, a word ending in a sandhi-modification is still described as a word. // KDd 3.154 //

children.text: tathāpi kaṭu karṇānāṃ kavayo na prayuñjate /
children.translated_text: Even so, poets do not employ [forms] that are harsh to the ears —

children.text: dhvajinī tasya rājñaḥ ketūdastajaladety adaḥ // KDd_3.155 //
children.translated_text: 'that king's army, with banners obscuring the clouds' — this [form is faulty]. // KDd 3.155 //

children.text: varṇānāṃ nyūnatādhikye gurulaghvayathāsthitiḥ /
children.translated_text: Where there is deficiency or excess of syllables, or incorrect placement of heavy and light [syllables],

children.text: yatra tad bhinnavṛttaṃ syād eṣa doṣaḥ suninditaḥ // KDd_3.156 //
children.translated_text: that is 'broken in meter' (<s>bhinnavṛtta</s>) — this fault is greatly censured. // KDd 3.156 //

children.text: indupādāḥ śiśirāḥ spṛśantīty ūnavarṇatā /
children.translated_text: 'The cool moonbeams touch' — this has a deficiency of syllables;

children.text: sahakārasya kisalayāny ārdrāṇīty adhikākṣaram // KDd_3.157 //
children.translated_text: 'the tender leaves of the mango tree are moist' — this has excess syllables. // KDd 3.157 //

children.text: kāmena bāṇā niśitā vimuktā mṛgekṣaṇāsv ity ayathāgurutvam /
children.translated_text: 'Sharp arrows released by <s>Kāma</s> at the deer-eyed women' — this has incorrect heaviness;

children.text: madanabāṇā niśitāḥ patanti mṛgekṣaṇāsv ity ayathālaghutvam // KDd_3.158 //
children.translated_text: 'the sharp arrows of <s>Madana</s> fall upon the deer-eyed women' — this has incorrect lightness. // KDd 3.158 //

children.text: na saṃhitāṃ vivakṣāmīty asaṃdhānaṃ padeṣu yat /
children.translated_text: When there is non-joining of words [where sandhi is required], saying 'I do not intend a compound form' —

children.text: tad visaṃdhīti nirdiṣṭaṃ na pragṛhyādihetukam // KDd_3.159 //
children.translated_text: that is designated 'defective sandhi' (<s>visaṃdhi</s>), not when caused by <s>pragṛhya</s> [vowels] and the like. // KDd 3.159 //

children.text: mandānilena caratā aṅganāgaṇḍamaṇḍale /
children.translated_text: 'By the gentle breeze moving on the cheeks of women,

children.text: luptam udbhedi gharmāmbho nabhasy asmanmanasy api // KDd_3.160 //
children.translated_text: the sweat that had disappeared rises again — in the sky and in our mind too.' // KDd 3.160 //

children.text: ādhivyādhiparītāya adya śvo vā vināśine /
children.translated_text: 'For a body beset by mental and physical afflictions, perishing today or tomorrow —

children.text: ko hi nāma śarīrāya dharmāpetaṃ samācaret // DKd_3.160* //
children.translated_text: who indeed would perform [any act] contrary to <s>dharma</s> for the sake of such a body?' // DKd 3.160* //

children.text: luptam udbhedi gharmāmbho nabhasy asmanmanasy api /
children.translated_text: 'The sweat that had disappeared rises again — in the sky and in our mind too;

children.text: āsu rātriṣv iti prājñair ajñātaṃ nyaṅgam īdṛśam // KDd_3.161 //
children.translated_text: in these nights' — such a defect, though unrecognized by the wise, is [nevertheless] a blemish. // KDd 3.161 //

body.text:
For the repetition of 160cd in 161ab, most editions read:
mānerṣye iha śīryete strīṇāṃ himaṛtau priye
body.translated_text: For the repetition of 160cd in 161ab, most editions read: pride and jealousy decay here for women in the winter season, O beloved

children.text: deśo 'drivanarāṣṭrādiḥ kālo rātriṃdivartavaḥ /
children.translated_text: Place (<s>deśa</s>) refers to mountains, forests, kingdoms, and so forth; time (<s>kāla</s>) refers to the cycle of nights and days;

children.text: nṛttagītaprabhṛtayaḥ kalāḥ kāmārthasaṃśrayāḥ // KDd_3.162 //
children.translated_text: the arts (<s>kalā</s>) include dance, song, and the like, which pertain to pleasure and wealth. (3.162)

children.text: carācarāṇāṃ bhūtānāṃ pravṛttir lokasaṃjñitā /
children.translated_text: The activity of beings both moving and stationary is termed worldly convention (<s>loka</s>);

children.text: hetuvidyātmako nyāyaḥ sasmṛtiḥ śrutir āgamaḥ // KDd_3.163 //
children.translated_text: logic (<s>nyāya</s>) consists of the science of reasoning (<s>hetuvidyā</s>); scripture (<s>āgama</s>) comprises <s>Smṛti</s> and <s>Śruti</s>. (3.163)

children.text: teṣu teṣv ayathārūḍhaṃ yadi kiṃ cit pravartate /
children.translated_text: If in any of these something proceeds contrary to established fact

children.text: kaveḥ pramādād deśādivirodhīty etad ucyate // KDd_3.164 //
children.translated_text: through the poet's carelessness, it is called a contradiction of place, etc. (<s>deśādi-virodha</s>). (3.164)

children.text: karpūrapādapāmarśasurabhir malayānilaḥ /
children.translated_text: The <s>Malaya</s> breeze is fragrant from contact with camphor trees;

children.text: kaliṅgavanasaṃbhūtā mṛgaprāyā mataṅgajāḥ // KDd_3.165 //
children.translated_text: elephants born in the forests of <s>Kaliṅga</s> are mostly like deer; (3.165)

children.text: colāḥ kālāgaruśyāmāḥ kāverītīrabhūmayaḥ /
children.translated_text: the lands along the banks of the <s>Kāverī</s> in <s>Cola</s> country are dark with black aloe-wood --

children.text: iti deśavirodhinyā vācaḥ prasthānam īdṛśam // KDd_3.166 //
children.translated_text: such is the manner of speech that contradicts place (<s>deśa-virodha</s>). (3.166)

children.text: padminī naktam unnidrā sphuṭaty ahni kumudvatī /
children.translated_text: The day-lotus blooms at night; the night-lily opens during the day;

children.text: madhur utphullaniculo nidāgho meghadurdinaḥ // KDd_3.167 //
children.translated_text: spring has blossoming <s>nicula</s> trees; summer has cloudy, rainy days; (3.167)

children.text: śravyahaṃsagiro varṣāḥ śarad āmattabarhiṇī /
children.translated_text: the rains have the pleasant calls of geese; autumn has intoxicated peacocks;

children.text: hemanto nirmalādityaḥ śiśiraḥ ślāghyacandanaḥ // KDd_3.168 //
children.translated_text: winter (<s>hemanta</s>) has a spotless sun; the cool season (<s>śiśira</s>) is praised for its sandalwood -- (3.168)

children.text: iti kālavirodhasya darśitā gatir īdṛśī /
children.translated_text: thus has the course of contradiction of time (<s>kāla-virodha</s>) been illustrated.

children.text: mārgaḥ kalāvirodhasya manāg uddiśyate yathā // KDd_3.169 //
children.translated_text: The path of contradiction of the arts (<s>kalā-virodha</s>) is briefly indicated as follows: (3.169)

children.text: vīraśṛṅgārayor bhāvau sthāyinau krodhavismayau /
children.translated_text: The permanent emotions (<s>sthāyibhāva</s>) of the heroic (<s>vīra</s>) and erotic (<s>śṛṅgāra</s>) <s>rasas</s> are anger and wonder;

children.text: pūrṇasaptasvaraḥ so 'yaṃ bhinnamārgaḥ pravartate // KDd_3.170 //
children.translated_text: this <s>rāga</s>, complete with all seven notes, proceeds in a different melodic path. (3.170)

children.text: itthaṃ kalācatuḥṣaṣṭau virodhaḥ sādhu nīyatām /
children.translated_text: Thus let contradiction be properly identified across the sixty-four arts;

children.text: tasyāḥ kalāparicchede rūpam āvirbhaviṣyati // KDd_3.171 //
children.translated_text: its form will become manifest in the detailed treatment of each art. (3.171)

children.text: ādhūtakesaro hastī tīkṣṇaśṛṅgas turaṅgamaḥ /
children.translated_text: An elephant with shaking mane-like tufts; a horse with sharp horns;

children.text: gurusāro 'yam eraṇḍo niḥsāraḥ khadiradrumaḥ // KDd_3.172 //
children.translated_text: this castor-oil plant is heavy-hearted; the <s>khadira</s> tree is without substance -- (3.172)

children.text: iti laukika evāyaṃ virodhaḥ sarvagarhitaḥ /
children.translated_text: this is a contradiction of worldly experience (<s>laukika virodha</s>), universally condemned.

children.text: virodho hetuvidyāsu nyāyākhyāsu nidarśyate // KDd_3.173 //
children.translated_text: Contradiction in the sciences of reasoning, called <s>nyāya</s>, is now illustrated: (3.173)

children.text: satyam evāha sugataḥ saṃskārān avinaśvarān /
children.translated_text: The <s>Sugata</s> (Buddha) truly declared that mental impressions (<s>saṃskāra</s>) are imperishable --

children.text: tathā hi sā cakorākṣī sthitaivādyāpi me hṛdi // KDd_3.174 //
children.translated_text: for indeed, that <s>cakorākṣī</s> (partridge-eyed woman) remains even now in my heart. (3.174)

children.text: kāpilair asadudbhūtiḥ sthāna evopavarṇyate /
children.translated_text: In the <s>Kāpila</s> (Sāṅkhya) system, origination from non-being (<s>asad-udbhūti</s>) is described as established --

children.text: asatām eva dṛśyante yasmād asmābhir udbhavāḥ // KDd_3.175 //
children.translated_text: since we ourselves observe the arising of non-existent things. (3.175)

children.text: nītir nyāyavirodhasya saiṣā sarvatra dṛśyatām /
children.translated_text: This is the method of contradiction of logic (<s>nyāya-virodha</s>); let it be observed everywhere.

children.text: athāgamavirodhasya prasthānaṃ darśayiṣyate // KDd_3.176 //
children.translated_text: Now the manner of contradiction of scripture (<s>āgama-virodha</s>) will be shown: (3.176)

children.text: anāhitāgnayo 'py ete jātaputrā vitanvate /
children.translated_text: These <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, though they have not established their sacred fires, having sons, perform

children.text: viprā vaiśvānarīm iṣṭim akliṣṭācārabhūṣaṇāḥ // KDd_3.177 //
children.translated_text: the <s>Vaiśvānarī</s> sacrifice, adorned with untroubled conduct. (3.177)

children.text: asāv anupanīto 'pi vedān adhijage guroḥ /
children.translated_text: That man, though uninitiated (<s>anupanīta</s>), studied the <s>Vedas</s> from a teacher --

children.text: svabhāvaśuddhaḥ sphaṭiko na saṃskāram apekṣate // KDd_3.178 //
children.translated_text: a crystal, pure by nature, does not require any polishing. (3.178)

children.text: virodhaḥ sakalo 'py eṣa kadā cit kavikauśalāt /
children.translated_text: Yet all this contradiction may sometimes, through the poet's skill,

children.text: utkramya doṣagaṇanāṃ guṇavīthīṃ vigāhate // KDd_3.179 //
children.translated_text: transcend the enumeration of faults and enter the path of virtues (<s>guṇa</s>). (3.179)

children.text: tasya rājñaḥ prabhāveṇa tadudyānāni jajñire /
children.translated_text: By the power of that king, his gardens came into being,

children.text: ārdrāṃśukapravālānām āspadaṃ suraśākhinām // KDd_3.180 //
children.translated_text: becoming abodes of celestial wish-granting trees (<s>suraśākhin</s>) with moist shoots and coral-like sprouts. (3.180)

children.text: rājñāṃ vināśapiśunaś cacāra kharamārutaḥ /
children.translated_text: A harsh wind, portending the destruction of kings, blew about,

children.text: dhunvan kadambarajasā saha saptacchadodgamān // KDd_3.181 //
children.translated_text: scattering along with <s>kadamba</s> pollen the emerging <s>saptacchada</s> blossoms. (3.181)

children.text: dolātipreraṇātrastavadhūjanamukhodgatam /
children.translated_text: The song rising from the faces of young brides frightened by the excessive swinging of swings,

children.text: kāmināṃ layavaiṣamyād geyaṃ rāgam avardhayat // KDd_3.182 //
children.translated_text: through its irregularity of rhythm, increased the passion of lovers. (3.182)

children.text: aindavād arciṣaḥ kāmī śiśiraṃ havyavāhanam /
children.translated_text: This lover, distressed and agitated by the anguish of separation from his beloved,

children.text: abalāvirahakleśavihvalo gaṇayaty ayam // KDd_3.183 //
children.translated_text: considers the fire (<s>Havyavāhana</s>) cool compared to the moonbeams. (3.183)

children.text: prameyo 'py aprameyo 'si sakalo 'py asi niṣkalaḥ /
children.translated_text: Though measurable, You are immeasurable; though whole, You are without parts;

children.text: ekas tvam apy aneko 'si namas te viśvamūrtaye // KDd_3.184 //
children.translated_text: though one, You are many -- salutations to You, O <s>Viśvamūrti</s> (Lord of universal form)! (3.184)

children.text: pañcānāṃ pāṇḍuputrāṇāṃ patnī pañcālakanyakā /
children.translated_text: The princess of <s>Pañcāla</s> was the wife of the five sons of <s>Pāṇḍu</s>,

children.text: satīnām agraṇīś cāsīd daivo hi vidhir īdṛśaḥ // KDd_3.185 //
children.translated_text: and yet she was the foremost among virtuous women -- for such is the decree of fate. (3.185)

children.text: śabdārthālaṃkriyāś citrā mārgāḥ sukaraduṣkarāḥ /
children.translated_text: The ornaments of word, meaning, and figuration; the marvelous modes both easy and difficult;

children.text: guṇā doṣāś ca kāvyānām iti saṃkṣipya darśitāḥ // KDd_3.186 //
children.translated_text: the virtues and faults of poetry -- all these have been shown in summary. (3.186)

children.text: vyutpannabuddhir amunā vidhidarśitena mārgeṇa doṣaguṇayor vaśavartinībhiḥ /
children.translated_text: One whose intellect is cultivated, following the path herein demonstrated, courted by speeches

children.text: vāgbhiḥ kṛtābhisaraṇo madirekṣaṇābhir dhanyo yuveva ramate labhate ca kīrtim // KDd_3.187 //
children.translated_text: that are obedient to both faults and virtues, like intoxicating-eyed women -- that fortunate one delights like a youth and attains fame. (3.187)

body.text: || ity ācāryaśrīdaṇḍinaḥ kṛtau kāvyādarśe duṣkaranāmā tṛtīyaḥ paricchedaḥ samāptaḥ ||
body.translated_text: Thus ends the third chapter, named 'Duṣkara' (The Difficult), in the <s>Kāvyādarśa</s> (Mirror of Poetry) composed by the revered master <s>Daṇḍin</s>.
